stages.title: Stage 26 — Reading Strategy
stages.subtitle: Systematic High-Level to Low-Level Source Traversal

details.title: Subsystem Reading Order
items: 3. Read AIDL / HIDL Binder interface contract
6. Read HAL Interface and Vendor implementation
7. Read Linux Kernel driver interaction (`ioctl` / sysfs)

details.title: Full Stack Call Chain Pipeline
items: Application → Framework API → Manager → Binder Proxy → Binder Driver → System Service → Native Library → HAL → Kernel → Hardware

details.title: Target Subsystem Traces to Master
items: Camera capture, Audio playback, Bluetooth pairing, Wi-Fi scanning, Notifications posting, Storage writing, Package installation, Activity launch, UI rendering, Location updates, Biometric authentication

details.title: Source Analysis Habits
items: Read interface contracts before reviewing concrete implementations
Understand high-level architecture before analyzing specific algorithms
Follow execution flow linearly instead of browsing randomly
Review Git commit history (`git log` / Gerrit) for design rationale
Compare API documentation with actual implementation behavior
Trace both success execution paths and error failure handling paths
Build architectural diagrams and call graphs while reading

details.title: Subsystem Reconstruction Framework
items: For every major AOSP subsystem, reconstruct:
• Architecture → Key Classes → Core Methods → Execution Flow → Binder Interfaces → Native Implementation → HAL → Kernel Interaction
Repeat exercise across: AMS, PMS, WMS, SurfaceFlinger, ART, Bionic, Netd, AudioFlinger, CameraService

details.title: Continuous Mastery Goals
items: Tracking new Android platform releases and AOSP commit changes
Monitoring ART compiler and GC improvements
Tracking Binder IPC enhancements and libbinder_ndk evolutions
Studying Project Mainline updatable APEX module expansions
Following Jetpack library evolution and framework integrations
Studying LLVM toolchain and compiler optimizations
Monitoring platform security architecture changes and mitigations

stages.title: Stage 31 — Expert-Level Mental Models
stages.subtitle: System Inquiry Checklist for Expert Analysis

details.title: Platform Expert Inquiry Checklist
items: Why is this framework API implemented in this specific way?
Which layer owns the ultimate responsibility for this operation?
Could this system behavior be implemented elsewhere in the stack?
Where does permission and capability enforcement occur?
Which Linux process executes this code (`system_server`, `app`, `daemon`)?
Which thread executes this callback (UI thread, Binder thread, RenderThread)?
Which memory region stores this object (Java Heap, Native Heap, Shared Memory)?
Which Binder transaction code and interface is involved?
Which native shared library (`.so`) is called via JNI or Binder?
Which HAL implementation is invoked (AIDL / HIDL)?
Which Linux kernel subsystem or driver finally performs the hardware operation?
